analysis.title: BofA Securities Equity Client Flow Trends: Selling by all client groups; more extreme Comm. Services outflows
key_insights: Clients sold US equities for the 3rd straight week (week of 10/26-10/30, S&P 500 -0.6%), led by single stock outflows of -$7.1bn. Clients bought equity ETFs ($2.4bn) for the 3rd straight week.

All major client groups were net sellers: hedge funds -$2.9bn, private clients -$1.6bn, institutional -$0.2bn (stocks plus equity ETFs). Hedge funds had their 3rd week of outflows and the biggest outflow week since mid-July.
Hedge funds' 4-week average net flows (stocks plus ETFs) turned negative for the first time in 3 months.
Clients bought small and mid cap equities and sold large caps. Large cap single stocks saw -$8.1bn last week, and large cap 4-week average flows have been negative for 6 straight weeks.

October institutional outflows, normalized by market cap, were the largest of any October in 9 years. BofA reads this as a big month for tax loss selling ahead of the 10/31 mutual fund deadline, and points to Theme Screens for tax loss candidates that could bounce in November.
Corporate client buybacks accelerated for the 5th week but remain slightly below seasonal averages. Annualized YTD buybacks are tracking below 2024-25 levels and above 2010-23 levels.
Rolling 52-week corporate buybacks as a % of S&P 500 market cap are 0.18%, the lowest since 2021, down from a 0.42% peak in Feb. 2025.

Communication Services had its 2nd straight week of record outflows since the GICS sector began in 9/2018, both in dollars and as a % of market cap. Single stock outflows were -$6.2bn last week versus -$4.8bn the prior week, coinciding with the sell-off around Google's results.

Within Comm. Services, hedge funds sold -$2.8bn, institutional clients -$2.3bn and private clients -$1.1bn of stocks. Comm. Services 4-week average outflows have now run for 3 straight weeks, at -$2.9bn versus a 52-week average of -$0.2bn.

Tech single stocks were sold for the 3rd week (-$1.1bn last week, 4-week average -$2.7bn), while Tech ETFs took in $591mn, the largest sector ETF inflow. Tech ETF 4-week average flows flipped positive.
Industrials have the longest selling streak at 14 weeks (the longest on record was 30 weeks in 2016). Last week Industrials stocks saw -$746mn.

Consumer Discretionary saw the largest sector inflows (+$1.3bn single stocks). Energy saw inflows for the 3rd straight week, and its 4-week average turned positive for the first time since early September.
Real Estate stocks saw -$660mn last week and 4-week average outflows for the first time since July. Financials 4-week average inflows are the first since September.

Equity ETFs saw inflows across Value, Blend and Growth styles and across all size segments except mid cap. All sectors except Real Estate and Materials saw ETF inflows. Blend ETFs led styles at +$1.7bn.

Hedge funds are net buyers of single stocks YTD (+$13.3bn) but 2025 saw -$29.9bn. Institutional clients are -$63.7bn and private clients -$54.8bn in single stocks YTD, for a total of -$105.2bn, against +$65.5bn into ETFs.
Institutional 4-week average single stock outflows have run for 6 straight weeks, and stock plus ETF outflows for 5 straight weeks.
Weekly sector flow z-scores: Communications is at -6.44 on a 5-year basis, Real Estate at -2.87, and Consumer Discretionary at +2.15.

trade_ideas.description: Buy tax loss candidates that could bounce in November, as screened in BofA's Theme Screens. No specific tickers are named in this report.
trade_ideas.rationale: Record October institutional selling suggests heavy tax loss selling, which could reverse after the 10/31 deadline.

risk_factors: Weekly flow data can be influenced by block trades and is more volatile than the 4-week average.
Hedge fund selling has broadened, with the 4-week average flipping negative.
Buybacks as a % of S&P 500 market cap are the lowest since 2021, reducing a source of demand.
The report states the flow data is not meant to be predictive of the market.
charts_described: Exhibit 3 plots institutional clients' net buying of single stocks as a % of S&P 500 market cap in Sept./Oct. by year, and the text states October 2026 outflows were the largest of any October in 9 years.
Exhibit 21 plots rolling 52-week corporate client buybacks as a % of S&P 500 market cap, which peaked at 0.42% in Feb. 2025 and is 0.18% now, the lowest since 2021.
vol_and_positioning: Hedge fund 4-week average net flows (stocks plus ETFs) turned negative for the first time in 3 months, and the 4-week average has been negative since July per Exhibit 41.
Hedge funds are net buyers over the past 12 months, but single stock selling of -$4.2bn last week was their largest outflow week since mid-July.
Institutional clients' October outflows were the largest of any October in 9 years, consistent with tax loss selling before the 10/31 mutual fund deadline.
Comm. Services weekly flow z-score is -2.20 versus 3 months, -3.51 versus 1 year and -6.44 versus 5 years.
Hedge funds' ETF flow z-scores are positive in Growth (+2.55 on 3m) and Technology (+2.52 on 3m), and Dividend ETFs are at +2.46 on 3m.
Institutional single stock 4-week average is -$1.5bn and private client single stock 4-week average is -$2.2bn.

tension_points.bull_case: Hedge funds are still net buyers of US equities over the past 12 months, and clients continue to buy equity ETFs, with Tech ETFs the largest sector ETF inflow last week.
tension_points.bear_case: Hedge funds' 4-week average net flows flipped negative for the first time in 3 months, with their largest outflow week since mid-July, and all client groups were net sellers.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Hedge funds' 4-week average net flows turning positive again, which would reverse the first negative reading in 3 months.
